events.title: RMS Titanic Departs Southampton
events.description: The RMS Titanic began her maiden voyage from Southampton, England, bound for New York City, with stops planned at Cherbourg, France, and Queenstown, Ireland. She carried over 2,200 passengers and crew.
events.significance: The voyage ended in tragedy on April 15, 1912, when the ship struck an iceberg and sank, killing more than 1,500 people and leading to major reforms in maritime safety regulations.

events.title: Eruption of Mount Tambora Begins Its Peak
events.description: The massive eruption of Mount Tambora on the island of Sumbawa in present-day Indonesia reached its climax on April 10, 1815, after beginning on April 5. It was the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history.
events.significance: The eruption killed tens of thousands directly and caused global climate disruption, leading to 1816 being known as the Year Without a Summer, with widespread crop failures and famine.

events.title: Good Friday Agreement Reached
events.description: After marathon negotiations led by US Senator George Mitchell, the British and Irish governments and most Northern Irish political parties agreed to the Good Friday (Belfast) Agreement.
events.significance: The agreement established a framework for power-sharing and largely brought an end to The Troubles, a decades-long conflict in Northern Ireland that had claimed over 3,500 lives.

events.title: Birth of William Booth
events.description: William Booth, the English Methodist preacher who founded The Salvation Army, was born in Sneinton, Nottingham, England.
events.significance: Booth built The Salvation Army into a global Christian charitable organization providing aid to the poor, homeless, and disadvantaged in over 130 countries.

events.title: The Great Gatsby Published
events.description: F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby was first published by Charles Scribner's Sons in New York.
events.significance: Initially a modest commercial success, the novel became regarded as one of the greatest works of American literature and a defining portrait of the Jazz Age and the American Dream.
